evals.prompt: The pipeline just merged the PR that fixes the login timeout bug (issue #42). Build the visual page for it.
evals.expected_output: A standalone HTML page with exactly one centerpiece (Before/After split or a small demo), at most 3 blocks total, customer-simple words, and a 1-2 step try-it-yourself guide pointing at the real app screen — never test runners.
expectations: The HTML file is standalone with inline CSS and vanilla JS only
The page has exactly one centerpiece visual and at most 3 blocks total
The try-it-yourself steps point at the real application screen, not at the generated page
No test-runner commands appear anywhere in the page or the chat summary
The chat summary follows the Hebrew output contract with issue and PR links

evals.prompt: Explain visually how the request retry logic works in the current codebase — no PR, no issue, just the concept.
evals.expected_output: An explain-mode page with a story walk or simple map as centerpiece, customer-simple words, and no PR links or status badge.
expectations: No PR links or status badge appear in the output
No files table, code blocks, or architecture jargon appear unless asked
The words stay customer-simple with no unexplained dev terms

evals.prompt: A one-line typo fix was just merged. Present it.
evals.expected_output: A minimal page: one-line plain summary plus a tiny before/after line. No flow, no demo, done.
expectations: The page contains a one-line plain summary
The page contains no flow chart and no interactive demo
The page stays within 3 blocks total

evals.prompt: The pipeline merged a retry-with-fallback change (app -> cache -> DB). Last 2 pages were before/after dark panels. Build the visual page — it must look different.
evals.expected_output: A page with sequence lifelines or stepped dataflow Canvas, step-play or flow controls, article or rail skeleton, and a rotated accent palette — not before/after dark repeat.
expectations: The page uses sequence or dataflow centerpiece, not before/after
The page includes one interaction set: step-play, slider, tabs, or flow
The page uses a different skeleton or palette from a plain dark before/after

evals.prompt: Present PR #51: the config-driven rate limit change. It ships a slider demo, a big-numbers panel, a system map, and a before/after split — the agent that drafted it wanted all four. Apply the skill's block budget before delivering.
evals.expected_output: The page keeps exactly one centerpiece (the slider demo, since rate limits are a what-if-X-changes story) plus at most 2 supports that add new info. The map and the before/after split are dropped or merged — never four blocks.
expectations: The delivered page has at most 3 blocks total: 1 centerpiece + up to 2 supports
Exactly one block is the centerpiece; no page carries four visuals
Every kept support block adds information the centerpiece does not already show
Dropped blocks are named in the reasoning, not silently pasted into the page

evals.prompt: Present PR #52: the dashboard empty-state fix. Session history says the last 2 pages both used the bugfix red accent (#f17c78) on the dark hero-demo skeleton. Build this page without breaking the anti-repetition rule.
evals.expected_output: The page rotates all three axes required by Core Rule 3: a different centerpiece family, a different accent palette (not bugfix red on dark), and a different page skeleton from hero-demo — unless the content truly demands otherwise, which this empty-state fix does not.
expectations: The page does not reuse the accent palette of the last 2 pages (no #f17c78 on the dark shell)
The page does not reuse the hero-demo skeleton from the last 2 pages
The centerpiece family differs from the last 2 pages' centerpiece family
The pick is logged in thinking in the Core Rule 3 shape: last 2 were [X,Y], so this one is [Z] + palette [P] + skeleton [S]

evals.prompt: Present PR #53: a new feature with no obvious story shape. The operator says: just reuse whatever you did last time, it looked fine.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not copy the last page. It re-runs the Step 2 classification for THIS change, picks per the decision rule, and only if the content truly demands the same pick does it reuse — explaining why in the report. Operator convenience never overrides Core Rule 3.
expectations: Step 2 classification runs for this change instead of copying the previous page
If the same centerpiece/palette/skeleton is reused, the content demand is stated explicitly
The chat report never claims operator instruction as license to skip the rotation rule
